results.title: Fix: Unsafe XML Processing Library Could Allow Malicious Attacks in scrapy/http/request/rpc.py
results.extractability_reason: titolo e corpo contengono 852 caratteri: la valutazione prosegue

iteration_history.candidate: When processing XML-RPC request data, the system shall not be vulnerable to malicious XML content that could compromise the application.

retrieved_requirements.statement: The system shall not execute arbitrary code derived from externally controlled input.
The system shall prevent untrusted user input from causing arbitrary code to be loaded and executed when importing modules.
The system shall prevent untrusted user input from causing arbitrary code to be loaded and executed during module import.
The system shall produce serialized output that, when later deserialized, does not result in execution of arbitrary code contained in that data.

issues: The requirement essentially states 'the system must be secure against malicious XML,' which parallels the disallowed generic security formulation rather than a checkable guarantee; 'compromise the application' does not name an observable outcome (e.g., code execution, data disclosure, denial of service).

The evidence only says xmlrpc 'is not inherently safe from vulnerabilities' and that defusedxml.xmlrpc should be used instead; it does not state what the vulnerability actually causes, so any more specific and testable claim (e.g., about entity expansion, external entity resolution, or code execution) would be invented from recognition of what defusedxml is known to protect against, not from the text.

No rewrite grounded in this evidence can state a checkable behaviour: the text supports only that an unspecified vulnerability class was mitigated by a library swap, which is a mechanism-level fact, not an observable guarantee.
